title: Fifth Canadian Soldier Dies Weeks After Tragic Base Fire
meta_title: Fifth Canadian Soldier Dies After CFB Wainwright Fire
meta_description: A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries sustained in an October wind-driven grass fire during a military training exercise at CFB Wainwright.
discover_titles: Fifth Canadian soldier dies after military base fire
Tragedy deepens as another soldier succumbs to CFB Wainwright fire injuries
Canadian military reports fifth death from October base fire
spot: A fifth Canadian soldier has succumbed to injuries sustained during an October grass fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, the military announced Saturday.
content_html:
Key Developments

Private William Douglas Dal Bianco passed away Friday at a hospital in Ontario, where he had been undergoing treatment following a severe wind-driven grass fire on October 17. The incident occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta during a military training exercise involving about 84 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.

The troops were conducting attack training on a grenade launcher range southeast of Edmonton when sudden wind shifts pushed flames from a grass fire directly toward the personnel. While Private Dal Bianco's passing brings the death toll to five, military officials confirmed that 24 other soldiers remain hospitalized.

Prime Minister Mark Carney paid tribute to the fallen service member on social media, emphasizing their dedication to defending the country. Military police are currently investigating the incident alongside a separate military board of inquiry tasked with examining the circumstances and recommending safety measures. Major General Wade Rutland noted that officials were aware of the fire for hours and believed it was contained before sudden wind shifts allowed the tragedy to unfold.

Key Takeaways

  • Private William Douglas Dal Bianco died Friday in an Ontario hospital from injuries sustained in the October 17 blaze.
  • The incident involved troops from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry during attack training at CFB Wainwright.
  • Twenty-four soldiers remain hospitalized as military police and a board of inquiry investigate the disaster.

Why It Matters

Prime Minister Carney has described the disaster as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil. The incident has prompted urgent scrutiny into military training safety protocols, communication regarding active fires during exercises, and emergency response procedures. As investigations continue, the high number of hospitalized personnel and the severe loss of life underscore the inherent risks faced by service members even during training operations within Canada.
